correctness.rationale: For k<=n+2, at most n+1 stationary elements yield 0, 1 or 2 forced completions in the moving sort. Two exist only if one other sort is doubled, in which case they are distinct by the quasigroup uniqueness axiom and no stationary candidate-sort element exists. With one completion, coincidence with the sole possible stationary candidate element is recorded by the fixed atomic diagram. All other candidates have a generic choice whenever orders are equal or both >=k. This provides an indefinite ordinary k-pebble bisimulation, with full equality/sort/relational preservation. Distinct-element sentences detect each order below k. At n+3, one intercalate sentence with n+3 variable names holds for cyclic additive cubes exactly when the cyclic order is even; choose odd/even orders both >=n+3. The two standalone finite examples at arities 2 and 3 were replayed from the actual embedded scripts; their limitation as finite tests is acknowledged.

originality.rationale: Actual published-record and literature queries were compared at the level of claims and implications. Existing algebraic work treats n-ary quasigroup decomposability; general finite-model-theoretic work provides the pebble method; Latin-square-graph work provides FO interpretations. None of the inspected relevant statements implies the claimed universal n+2-variable order-truncation classification or its sharp intercalate obstruction. Closest published Latin hypercube record concerns homotopy. This remains qualified against unindexed stronger results.
residual_risks: Search of published-finding corpus records is not a proof of exhaustive novelty.
A general theorem for partial Latin hypercubes or distance-two MDS code automorphism games might subsume the n+2 cutoff without naming it.
A relevant higher-arity logic result in uninspected sections or unindexed literature might change historical priority.

value.rationale: A complete natural classification holds simultaneously for all finite n-ary quasigroups across all arities and orders in the first n+2 variable widths, despite nonisotopic structure; the exact bound fails one width later for each arity via a uniform algebraic obstruction. The theorem exposes an arity-dependent logical expressive-power boundary and determines the count of theories exactly rather than giving a routine finite table or small numerical improvement.
